levels.title: Chip Fight
levels.summary: An indestructible horizontal ball blocks the single corridor before a mandatory chip.

levels.title: Ladder
levels.summary: The sole exit lies across a full-height permanent wall.

levels.title: Empty Islands
levels.summary: A mouse click replaces the invalid diagonal in the earlier replay. The corrected MS replay uses ordinary keyboard commands and one visible-tile click, collects all four chips, and completes at tick 920 in native Tile World and TWO with identical traces.

levels.title: Wait
levels.summary: Every released glider follows a fixed route into fire before reaching the green button.

levels.title: Number Soup
levels.summary: A keyless green door seals at least five needed chips; both exit routes remain closed.

levels.title: Altar
levels.summary: Neither DAT layer contains an Exit tile.

levels.title: Bloboy
levels.summary: A keyless green-door cut separates Chip from the exit.

levels.title: Escape from the Dungeon
levels.summary: Winning MS replay verified in both the TypeScript runtime and native Tile World: 3111 steps, final tick 3110.

levels.title: Bug island
levels.summary: Four chips lie inside an immutable fire ring, with no fire boots.

levels.title: Unlok the Blok
levels.summary: Mandatory chips under the bottom water channel cannot be exposed.

levels.title: Wait II (In Hell)
levels.summary: The maze containing the only green button has no mobile actor and an unconnected cloner.

levels.title: Buggy Day
levels.summary: Every required chip is separated from Chip by an unbridgeable water moat.

levels.title: Saturn
levels.summary: Both exits are inaccessible: one is sealed by permanent walls, and a south-force barrier prevents reaching the red key needed for the other. Blocks cannot provide a safe backstop.

levels.title: Marsupilami Block
levels.summary: Investigation is continuing; no winning replay or complete impossibility argument is established yet.

levels.title: Bazzar
levels.summary: At least 46 red keys are needed for the start gate and nine mandatory chip alcoves, but only 45 red keys exist.

levels.title: Leve5
levels.summary: A remote glider reverses a tank into a decorative Swimming Chip on tick32, killing the game before the player can intervene or exit.

levels.title: Adventures of Freddy 21
levels.summary: Two mandatory chip alcoves require a perpendicular turn on plain ice; the ice axis cannot change at their only approach.

levels.title: Tough Dirt Scramble
levels.summary: Neither map layer contains an Exit tile.

levels.title: Lost in Letterland III
levels.summary: Investigation is continuing; no winning replay or complete impossibility argument is established yet.

levels.title: whileuwait
levels.summary: Permanent walls and unconnected traps limit every potentially winning route to at most 36 chips, below the 131 required by the exit socket.

levels.title: RUN! III
levels.summary: Ten chips are permanently buried under frozen blocks; at most 384 of the required 385 can be collected.

levels.title: Diamonds II
levels.summary: Neither map layer contains an Exit tile.

levels.title: Somewhat Tedious II
levels.summary: The sole exit is buried under water behind a permanent block-delivery obstruction. Swimming destroys the buried exit instead of opening it.

levels.title: AGE DJ
levels.summary: 599 of 621 chips required; layered fake walls, bomb-covered chips and block cloners require a constructive route. Secondary exit is walled off.

levels.title: RUN!!! IV
levels.summary: Unresolved. A corrected MS route has collected 959 of the required 999 chips and matches native C at every recorded step. The final 40-chip route is still being constructed.

levels.title: Running BomberMan
levels.summary: A winning MS replay clears all 130 bombs with cloned blocks, collects the buried chips, and exits at tick 18,780. The native and TypeScript traces match exactly.

levels.title: The Nab II
levels.summary: The only passages out of the upper area strip the sole fire boots, making return to the exit lethal. Staying inside yields at most 317 of 411 required chips.

levels.title: The Nab III
levels.summary: Neither map plane contains an Exit tile, and MS gameplay cannot create one.

levels.title: Splash Splesh Splish Splosh Spulsh
levels.summary: Neither map plane contains an Exit tile, and MS gameplay cannot create one.

levels.title: Extremely Tough Jumping Swarm!
levels.summary: 376 of 419 chips required. Extra chips permit bypassing some inaccessible-looking pockets, so a local obstruction alone is insufficient.

levels.title: Look the Editor II
levels.summary: 246 required chips lie on unconnected beartraps; collecting any one permanently traps Chip away from the exit.

levels.title: Stalker
levels.summary: Four required chips are permanently sealed behind immutable walls; both exits lie behind the socket requiring all 36 chips.

levels.title: Variations I
levels.summary: The required chip at (10,8) can be collected, but doing so consumes the only ice pivot and traps Chip permanently in a closed cross.

levels.title: Variations II
levels.summary: The required chip at (10,8) can be collected, but doing so consumes the only ice pivot and traps Chip permanently in a closed cross.

levels.title: A Bit Walkery
levels.summary: A native-verified partial replay collects 1,914 of the 1,940 required chips and remains alive at tick 9675. The final chips around the walker cloner remain unresolved; no winning replay or complete impossibility argument is established.

levels.title: Green Kittens Aren't Aliens
levels.summary: Native-verified partial route collects five of 16 chips by tick 227 and parks a freed teeth against the east thin wall at (21,20). Eleven chips remain; no winning replay or impossibility proof yet.

levels.title: Key Maze
levels.summary: The only green key is trapped behind green doors or the all-chip socket, while eight mandatory chips themselves require a green key. The exit also requires green.

levels.title: Dancing with the Stars
levels.summary: Neither map plane contains an Exit tile, and MS gameplay cannot create one.
